title: Thresholded Composite Target Controller for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a controller that composes multiple throughput targets (short-horizon p95/p99, sustained avg, and class-weighted concurrency targets) into a single autoscaling setpoint, with an independent safety limiter that enforces ramp-rate, absolute capacity floors, and proportional tenant isolation fences. This ticket covers the algorithm, config model, runtime integration, API surface for Dedicated customers, and a conservative rollout plan with observability and guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Controller accepts a config with: horizons (short/med/long), percentile weights, class weights, and safety limits
Controller computes a single target throughput per-tenant and aggregate fleet setpoint that matches reference simulator outputs within 5% on benchmark traces
Safety limiter blocks any scale action that would exceed configured ramp-rate or violate per-tenant isolation budgets
Integration tests exercising burst and sustained scenarios pass in CI (latency SLOs preserved)
Console shows per-tenant composed target, contributing signals breakdown, and latest safety limiter state
technical_notes: We use a composite scoring function: score = sum_i w_i * normalize_i(metric_i) where normalize_i is a percentile -> throughput mapping derived from offline regression on historical traces
Short-horizon percentiles (p95/p99) get exponentially higher weight under fast-increase conditions; sustained avg weights grow with forecasted load persistence
To avoid noise amplification, apply Tukey-style winsorization on metric inputs and a small additive Laplace smoothing term to prevent zero-division in normalization
Safety limiter runs as a separate synchronous check: it enforces three constraints (ramp_rate, absolute_min_capacity, tenant_proportional_limit) and returns a trimmed target when necessary
Runtime will expose two decision traces for each evaluation: proposed_target and post_safety_target for auditing and replay
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype the composite scoring algorithm in Python using representative traces from prod-sim and notebook the parameter sweep
Week 2: Translate algorithm to Go runtime module with pluggable normalizers and unit tests; add feature flag gating
Week 3: Implement safety limiter module (ramp, floor, proportional isolation) and wire into the decision path with atomic compare-and-swap to prevent racey scale commits
Week 4: Add telemetry (contribution breakdown, limiter hits, rejected_scale_count) and dashboard mockups in Console; write integration tests against kube/gke-like cluster sim
Week 5: Canary rollout to a small Dedicated fleet with auto-rollback on limiter violations or SLO regressions, then iterate on weights and thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization functions and weight composition with expected numeric outputs
Property-based tests to ensure monotonicity of composed target with respect to each input metric
Integration test harness using archived traffic traces: compare proposed vs baseline autoscaler under bursty and sustained patterns
Chaos test where safety limiter drops connectivity to a subset of nodes; ensure controller respects proportional isolation limits and records limiter events
Performance test to validate decision latency under 10k tenant evaluations per second (target < 25ms decision path)
rollout_notes: Gate behind feature flag and /alpha API so we can enable per-customer; default to legacy autoscaler for all existing fleets
Canary stage 1: 3 non-production fleets with synthetic traffic for 72h; monitor limiter_hits, latency SLO, and rejected_scale_count
Canary stage 2: 5 low-risk customer fleets for 7 days with read-only telemetry shared with SEs; collect feedback
Full rollout: enable on new Dedicated fleets and gradually opt-in existing fleets via Console toggle; allow rollback to legacy decision path within 15 minutes
